contentBlocks.body: A class defines an object with identity and behavior. A constructor establishes its initial state; properties expose controlled access to that state. Here the Product constructor assigns a SKU and starting stock to read-only properties. Every new Product call creates a separate object. Contrast this identity with the value equality supplied by the record from the earlier lesson. Revisit this class before using EF Core entities in the project track.

**Trace the contract.** In the first case, the input is ["A",3]. The required result is "A:3". Before running code, explain which input values contribute to the result and which are excluded. Then change one boundary value and predict whether the result changes.

**Your task.** Construct a Product from the arguments, then return its SKU and Stock joined by a colon.
A static field is shared by the type; it is not independent state for each product.

**Check your understanding.** Why might a private setter protect stock better than a public field? Write the reason in your own words before opening the solution. Run the additional cases as well as the visible example: the zero stock case checks a different boundary.

**Transfer it.** Use an entity constructor to establish a valid initial state, then expose explicit adjustment behavior.

knowledgeItems.prompt: When does the Product constructor run?

choices: When new Product creates an instance
payload.answer: When new Product creates an instance
payload.explanation: The constructor establishes instance state once during creation.
